purpose: Finasteride is used to treat an enlarged prostate in men, which can make it hard to urinate. It is also used at a lower dose to treat male pattern hair loss (baldness). Your doctor will tell you which condition this medicine is meant to help you with.
how_it_works: Your body makes a hormone called DHT (dihydrotestosterone) that can cause your prostate to grow too large or your hair follicles to shrink. Finasteride blocks the enzyme that converts testosterone into DHT, so less DHT is made in your body. With lower DHT levels, the prostate can shrink over time, or hair loss can slow down or stop.
common_side_effects: Some men notice a lower sex drive, trouble getting or keeping an erection, or a decrease in the amount of semen released during sex. These effects are usually mild and may go away after your body adjusts to the medicine. Some men also notice breast tenderness or slight breast enlargement.
warnings: Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should never handle crushed or broken finasteride tablets, as the medicine can be absorbed through the skin and may harm an unborn baby. This medicine is for men only. Finasteride can lower your PSA level, which is a blood test used to screen for prostate cancer, so always remind your doctor you are taking it before any PSA testing. In rare cases, some men have reported that sexual side effects continued even after stopping the medicine, so talk to your doctor if you have concerns.
typical_dosing: For an enlarged prostate (Proscar), the usual dose is one 5 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. For hair loss (Propecia), the usual dose is one 1 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. It can take 3 to 6 months or longer before you notice the full benefit, so be patient and keep taking it as directed.
